title: Ligatures and the mouthpieces Kelly used
summary: Ligatures are mostly French; Kelly describes his Selmer mouthpieces, the Dixie-Beal special and string ligatures.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well Joe Clancy is famous, the stories about him. Yeah. Francis Murray, who you probably don't remember, he was a young man, and a saxophone player where he used to play stories about Joe Clancy. Well anyway, was there any special sort of ligature you used to, or that people generally use since you worked in the store?

Ligatures, most all of them are made in France, and there are different names put on them. The banal, the O-N-A-B-E, is what I actually used. But there are so many different variations of them. I just recently sent one that I got to put Brown in the water. And, Bud, I knew in St. Louis, his brother lives here in town. And he, I had this patented special ligature made by Gigliotti, he's a famous plant editor, and it was good, but I didn't find a big picture of the difference. It was made of plastic, and I had a certain image. I just sent it to Bud with the hope that maybe he could use it. He's experimenting around all the time.
I've even seen people pass string around there. Were you to believe in that?
The old theater clarinists back there, they used to take Fred. Yeah, Black Fred. And, and that was, now that's a purist for you.
Yeah. And, what kind of mouthpieces did you all use?

Oh, well, I, of course I always, I used a Selmer Table D, hard rubber mouthpiece for a long period of years. I hadn't become that technical until I got to where I really was interested in learning how to play. But, I then got a Dix to Beal back by 1935. Dix to Beal is in New Orleans, now director of the office at the World War was a hotel. But, anyhow, he had, he was very popular with Ben Burney at this time. And, so the wood-winning people put out this Dix to Beal special. I used that thing for 25 years. I was crazy. And, I dropped it from my office one day and broke it. And, so what I'm using now is Mitchell LeRae. And, Mitchell LeRae is a famous kind of teacher in California. That's the kind of reads I use now. And, Doran's became so unreliable that you'd have to buy a box to get one or two. Incidentally, with our good friend, Pinasako, he still doesn't, he'll buy a box to get one out of it. But, that's the, that's the one you've seen over there.
